titre: Written context becomes the raw material of design with agents
essentiel: Figma announces Specs: markdown on the canvas, designed as a container for context, fed via MCP and GitHub (open beta in the coming weeks).
Design systems have a new consumer, AI agents, and Design Systems Unfiltered publishes a first guide to making them usable by agents.
On the agent UX side, a permission pattern worth remembering: show what will change, why the agent is asking, that it can be undone, and let people say no calmly.

syntheses.titre: Figma makes written context an object on the canvas
syntheses.texte: With Specs, Figma presents markdown as a new medium on the canvas, a container for context that flows through MCP, GitHub and other tools. Written context (intentions, rules, specs) stops being a side document. One reply to the post asks whether an agent will be able to write back into a Spec via MCP, and the answer doesn't appear in what I was able to read.

syntheses.titre: Design systems now have AI as a user
syntheses.texte: Érica Menin starts from the observation that AI agents are a consumer of design systems, and that this isn't really new anymore. Her article covers the first steps to make them usable by AI. Read alongside Specs, it shows that machine-readable documentation is becoming a central workstream.

syntheses.titre: Agent permission patterns are real design work
syntheses.texte: Lisa Demchenko takes the example of The Drive AI, which shows a plan before acting and keeps changes reversible: an almost mundane preview-then-execute, and that's a compliment. She sees these as design decisions and would like to see more designers in these discussions. The pattern she keeps: what will change, why the agent is asking, that it can be undone, and a calm way to decline.

tendances.titre: Design systems now have AI as a user

tendances.titre: Agent permission patterns are real design work
tendances.texte: Previewing, explaining, allowing people to undo and to decline: these interface choices are a matter of design, not just engineering.
